guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.title: Houses Demolished and Occupants Moved Out Inside Guizhou's Protected Heritage Sites
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.place: Jiuzhou town, Huangping county, Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture, with sites in Taijiang and Jinping counties and Xingyi, Guizhou province, China
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.point: Jiuzhou town, Huangping county, the site where 65 traditional houses were renovated and their occupants moved out (OpenStreetMap place point for 旧州镇, Huangping county, Qiandongnan prefecture)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-76930-CN for CN-Guizhou Cultural and Natural Heritage Protection and Development (P091950). US$60 million approved 5 May 2009, effective 16 September 2009, of which US$59,167,978 was disbursed. Original closing 30 June 2016, actual closing 30 June 2017. Borrower financing rose from US$30 million to US$34.85 million and total project cost from US$90 million to US$94,017,978. Environmental category A; the policies triggered were Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01), Physical Cultural Resources (OP/BP 4.11), Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12) and Indigenous Peoples (OP/BP 4.10). The borrower was the International Department of China's Ministry of Finance and the implementing agency the Guizhou Tourism Development Commission. The completion report rates Involuntary Resettlement Satisfactory and the overall outcome Satisfactory on a split rating, with the original objective rated Moderately Unsatisfactory and the revised objective Highly Satisfactory (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004154, 18 December 2017, data sheet and paragraphs on safeguards and overall outcome). The Independent Evaluation Group's review ICRR0021065 rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, and rates the original objective Moderately Unsatisfactory and the revised objective Satisfactory.

companies.name: Guizhou Tourism Development Commission
companies.role: The provincial government body that implemented the project, through a provincial project management office (PPMO) and county-level offices in Anshun, Qiandongnan and Qianxinan prefectures. It is the Guizhou provincial administration's department for tourism, and it held responsibility for the renovation works at the heritage sites and for carrying out the resettlement plan (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 18 December 2017).

guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.community: The project paid for conservation and infrastructure works at cultural and natural heritage sites across Guizhou. Twelve houses, with a total building area of 3,178.3 square metres, and one unit of 2,000 square metres were demolished. Twelve households were resettled: four in Xingyi under the Wanfenglin subcomponent, with 720 square metres of wooden housing replaced by 1,660 square metres of brick-concrete housing; one household of 151.65 square metres in Jinping under the Longli subcomponent, replaced by 200 square metres; and seven households in Taijiang whose 306.62 square metres of auxiliary structures were demolished for the renovation of Family Liu's ancestral hall, who received miscellaneous rooms and cash compensation. Taijiang county also demolished the judicial office and police station and relocated some staff from a staff dormitory, 2,000 square metres in total. The resettlement plan had provided for 1,064 households and 17,736 square metres to be demolished; the actual demolition area was 17.9 per cent of that, which the completion report attributes to implementation plan adjustments. Land acquisition affected 415 households, of which 245 were ethnic minority households and 170 Han. The project occupied 993.1 mu of land against 1,445.53 mu planned, of which 149.8 mu of collectively owned land was acquired, 676.8 mu of collectively owned land was taken by other means including leasing, and 166.5 mu was state-owned. The completion report states that 68.15 per cent of the occupied land was walking paths, drainage ditches, open spaces and flood lands owned collectively by villagers. Separately, at the project's mid-term review the Bank found that at Huangping Jiuzhou the renovation of 65 traditional houses had caused the temporary resettlement of their occupants, who included small farmers and shopkeepers, without the procedures the project's own Resettlement Policy Framework required. That framework states that people temporarily resettled for renovation work are to be treated as affected persons, should receive appropriate compensation, and that a resettlement plan, or a short plan where fewer than 200 people are affected, should be prepared, reviewed by the Bank and disclosed before the renovation work begins. The completion report says the issue was remedied afterwards through a due diligence report including a short plan, and through interviews verifying that the affected people had been treated and compensated appropriately. The completion report also records that compensation for the affected land and houses complied with provincial regulations and was higher than the resettlement plan provided, that total land acquisition and resettlement compensation came to 5.9 million yuan, that a sample survey of 58 households and 273 people found incomes after resettlement at 145.3 per cent of incomes before, and that of 114 people interviewed on construction satisfaction, 105 were satisfied, 9 basically satisfied and none dissatisfied. Some project villages, named as Shidong, Wubao and Zhanliu, saw compensation expenditure rise because of later project delays and the demands of affected people.
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.displaced_label: 12 households resettled, from the Bank's completion report table comparing planned and actual housing resettlement
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 1,337 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report counts 12 households resettled and 12 houses plus one unit demolished, against a resettlement plan that had provided for 1,064 households. A further 415 households were affected by land acquisition without being moved, and the occupants of 65 traditional houses at Huangping Jiuzhou were temporarily moved out during renovation without a count of people given.
guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.outcome: The loan closed on 30 June 2017, a year late, fully disbursed to US$59.17 million of US$60 million. The completion report of 18 December 2017 rates Involuntary Resettlement Satisfactory and the overall outcome Satisfactory on a split rating; the Independent Evaluation Group's review rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory. The review states of the four safeguard policies triggered that 'These safeguard issues were addressed in the ICR but there was no explicit evidence that project management had complied with these safeguards.' In 2016 UNESCO recognised the Lie Ancestral Hall Preservation and Renovation Project carried out under the project for its restoration processes and techniques.

guizhou-heritage-sites-demolition.confidence_note: The counts of houses demolished, households resettled and land acquired, and the finding about the 65 houses at Huangping Jiuzhou, come from the Bank's own completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of it, so the lender is reporting on its own project. No independent press report, court record, audit or field study of the resettlement at these sites was found, including in a Chinese-language search of the Huangping Jiuzhou site name. The two Bank documents differ on the Huangping Jiuzhou finding: the completion report says the renovation went ahead 'without the appropriate procedures set forth in the RPF', placing the fault in non-compliance with the framework, while the review calls it 'A shortcoming of the Resettlement Policy Framework was that it did not include appropriate procedures for the temporary resettlement of small scale farmers and shopkeepers', placing the fault in the framework's content. The review prints no date; the date given is the Bank's document date field. The completion report disagrees with itself on disbursement: its data sheet gives US$59,167,978 actually disbursed of the US$60 million loan, while its financial management paragraph says 'the loan amount of US$ 60 million was fully disbursed at loan closing.'

kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.title: Buildings Pulled Down and About 600 Households Moved for Kunming Metro Line 3
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.place: The section between Jinmasi and Dashuying stations on Metro Line 3, Kunming, Yunnan province, China
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.point: Jinmasi, Guandu district, Kunming, one end of the section where the buildings were dismantled (OpenStreetMap point for 金马寺, Jinma subdistrict, Guandu district, Kunming)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-80370 for the China: Kunming Urban Rail Project (P117656). US$300 million approved 10 May 2011, effective 19 October 2011; the commitment was revised to US$276,926,592 and that amount was disbursed. Original closing 30 November 2016, actual closing 30 June 2018, an extension the Evaluation Group's review puts at 19 months and the completion report's own economic analysis calls 18 months. Total project cost rose from US$1,711,600,000 to US$1,803,926,592, the balance funded by the borrower. The borrower was the International Department of China's Ministry of Finance and the implementing agency the Kunming Rail Transit Group Co., Ltd., changed at the restructuring of 23 November 2015. Environmental category A; Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12) was triggered. The completion report rates social safeguards performance satisfactory and the overall outcome Satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group's review ICRR0021559 also rates the outcome Satisfactory (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004604, 28 December 2018, data sheet and paragraphs 58, 68 and 44; IEG ICR Review ICRR0021559).

companies.name: Kunming Rail Transit Group Co., Ltd.
companies.role: The municipally owned company that built and operates the Kunming metro and was the project's implementing agency. It carried out the consultations and negotiations with the affected people and the resettlement under the project's Resettlement Action Plan, and it worked with the design consultants to reduce the number of houses demolished. The completion report records that the project's results indicators had to be revised at restructuring partly because the company itself was restructured (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 28 December 2018, data sheet and paragraphs 59 and 68).

kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.community: The loan paid for part of Metro Line 3, including stations and the Shizui depot. The Resettlement Action Plan counted 837 residential households and 108 enterprises affected, a figure the Evaluation Group's review repeats and attributes to design work that had already been done to reduce the number of demolitions. Between Jinmasi and Dashuying stations the tunnel was to have been bored by machine, but a detailed site survey found that the ground conditions and the age of the buildings would not permit it, so a cut-and-cover method was adopted that required several buildings to be dismantled. The completion report records 'problems encountered in relocation of about 600 households from the site between Jinmasi and Dashuying stations' and that 'The relocation of households living in these buildings took more than two years, resulting in the delayed construction at this site.' At the mid-term review of October 2014 the Bank recorded that difficulties in reaching agreement with affected people kept delaying the full implementation of the resettlement plans. Resettlement was completed at the end of April 2018 against an original date of December 2015; the Evaluation Group's review puts the delay at 28 months and attributes it to the change in technical features and to protracted negotiations with affected people. The completion report states that all affected households had moved into new replacement buildings by the end of the project and that all affected people had been fully paid resettlement compensation; the review states that compensation had been paid in full. The completion report also records that the project's social safeguards risk was rated low during preparation and the first two years of implementation, which both documents call over-optimistic given that the project was substantially delayed by resettlement, and that the loan closing date extension was due in part to the time it took to resolve the resettlement compensation claims.
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.displaced_label: about 600 households relocated from the site between Jinmasi and Dashuying stations, from the Bank's completion report
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 808 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report gives 'about 600 households' relocated from the Jinmasi to Dashuying site, and separately counts 837 residential households and 108 enterprises affected across the project. Neither document says how the 600 and the 837 overlap, and neither gives a count of people.
kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.outcome: The loan closed on 30 June 2018, 19 months late, with US$276.93 million of the US$300 million disbursed and the commitment cut to that amount. Resettlement finished at the end of April 2018, 28 months behind the original date. The completion report of 28 December 2018 rates the overall outcome Satisfactory and social safeguards performance satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group's review also rates the outcome Satisfactory. Both documents record as a lesson that station and shaft locations should be chosen to reduce the dismantling of existing structures and the relocation of households, and that a sound geotechnical survey is needed to avoid the kind of late design change that caused this relocation.

Independent Evaluation Group, ICR Review, CN-Kunming Urban Rail (P117656), Report No. ICRR0021559

kunming-line-3-jinmasi-relocation.confidence_note: The whole account rests on the Bank's own completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's review of that report, so the lender is reporting on its own project. No independent press report, court record, audit or field study of the Jinmasi to Dashuying relocation was found. Both Bank documents state that all affected households moved into new replacement buildings and that compensation was paid in full; what the documents record as going wrong is the two-year delay, the late design change that caused the demolitions and the under-rating of the social risk. The figure of about 600 households appears once, in the completion report's account of why construction was delayed, and the report does not say how it relates to the 837 households counted in the resettlement plan. The review prints no date; the date given is the Bank's document date field. Three figures differ inside the two documents. The completion report's data sheet gives the loan commitment revised to US$276,926,592 from US$300 million, a reduction of US$23.07 million, while its economic analysis says 'Only US$2 million of the initial loan was not utilized during project implementation.' The review puts the closing extension at 19 months, which matches the dates of 30 November 2016 and 30 June 2018 on the data sheet, while the completion report's economic analysis calls it 18 months. The review puts the resettlement delay at 28 months; the completion report gives the dates of December 2015 and end of April 2018 without naming a figure.

hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.title: Houses Pulled Down in Small Towns Across Hunan and Gansu
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.place: Cangshuipu town, Heshan district, Yiyang city, Hunan province, with sites in Hanshou, Loudi, Wangcheng, Miluo, Hengnan and Taoyuan in Hunan and in Qingyang, Tianshui and Zhangye in Gansu province, China
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.point: Cangshuipu town, Heshan district, Yiyang city, the single largest demolition the project itself caused in Hunan at 7,876 square metres and 41 households (OpenStreetMap place point for 沧水铺镇, Heshan district, Yiyang)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Three loans for the CN Integrated Economic Development of Small Towns project (P118597), US$50 million each for activities in Guangdong (IBRD-81610), Hunan (IBRD-81600) and Gansu (IBRD-81570), US$150 million in total, approved 24 May 2012 and effective 5 November 2012. Disbursement was US$49,655,102, US$49,938,994 and US$48,834,116 respectively, US$148,428,212 in total. Original closing 31 December 2017, actual closing 31 December 2018. Total project cost fell from US$296,640,000 to US$213,180,622. Environmental category B; five safeguard policies were triggered, among them Indigenous Peoples (OP 4.10) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). The borrower was the People's Republic of China and the implementing agencies were the provincial project management offices of Hunan, Gansu and Guangdong. The completion report rates relevance high, efficacy modest and efficiency substantial; the Independent Evaluation Group's review ICRR0021894 rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00004709, 24 September 2019, data sheet, paragraphs 98 to 99 and Annex 7; IEG ICR Review ICRR0021894).

companies.name: Hunan Provincial Project Management Office
companies.role: One of the three provincial government project offices that implemented the project, each a unit set up within its provincial administration to run the Bank-financed works in its own towns. The Hunan office commissioned the third-party external resettlement monitoring on which the completion report's Hunan demolition figures rest and oversaw the land acquisition and house demolition in Cangshuipu, Wanbao, Taizimiao, Dingziwan, Xinshi, Santang and Zoushi towns (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 24 September 2019, data sheet and Annex 7).

companies.name: Gansu Provincial Project Management Office
companies.role: The equivalent provincial government office in Gansu, which oversaw the land acquisition and house demolition in Hongwansi, Ganquan, Zaojiao and Dongzhi towns and commissioned the third-party external resettlement monitoring reports for that province (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 24 September 2019, data sheet and Annex 7).

hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.community: The project paid for roads, water supply, wastewater treatment and other works in small towns in three provinces. In Hunan 82 households were affected by house demolition, with 16,681.1 square metres pulled down against 20,689 square metres planned, and the completion report's table counts 321 people against 382 planned. The largest sites were Cangshuipu town of Yiyang, 7,876 square metres and 41 households, and Wanbao town of Loudi, 4,846 square metres and 24 households; Taizimiao town of Hanshou lost 2,800 square metres and 10 households, Dingziwan Street of Wangcheng 312.6 square metres and one household, and single households were affected at Xinshi town of Miluo and Santang town of Hengnan. At Zoushi town of Taoyuan county the project took 0.957 mu of the site of a bankrupt shoe factory owned by the town government, which had 58 former employees, and demolished 846.6 square metres. In Gansu 243 households were affected by house demolition, with 22,085 square metres pulled down against 21,165.7 square metres planned, and the table counts 681 people against 723 planned. Of that, 230 households, 613 people and 12,355.7 square metres were at Hongwansi town of Zhangye, where the completion report records that 'Resettlement and compensation completed before project kick-off. A due diligence report was prepared.' The remaining Gansu demolition was at Dongzhi town of Qingyang, 9,560.8 square metres against 7,420 planned and 11 households, and single households at Ganquan and Zaojiao towns of Tianshui. Planned demolition at Huahai town of Yumen and Dangzhai town of Ganzhou did not take place because project activities were adjusted. Land acquisition affected 471 households in Hunan, where 710.1 mu was planned and the actual occupation was slightly lower, and 640 households in Gansu, where 291.9 mu was planned and the actual occupation rose to 320.5 mu. The third-party consultants who monitored the resettlement concluded that the resettlement plans were followed on compensation standards, that all affected residents were properly resettled, that the size and quality of the relocation housing exceeded the original housing, and that compensation for land acquisition and house demolition was not lower than the plan specified. The same paragraph then records that 'there were delays in the land acquisition process as well as in providing compensation in some towns in Gansu and Hunan, which resulted in significant delays of project activities' - the consequence the report names for those delays is to the project's own works, not to the households. Wenfeng town in Gansu was dropped from the project altogether because of what the completion report calls unsolvable land and resettlement issues. In Guangdong the provincial office reported that all the project land was state-owned and that no physical resettlement would be needed; the Bank required an external evaluator to check whether anyone was adversely affected, and that report, submitted in January 2019, identified no particular issues. At Yuecheng town in Guangdong the completion report records that after almost two years of consultation, 38 households still did not want to take part in the project and their houses were left intact.
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.displaced_label: households whose houses were demolished, from the Bank's completion report tables comparing planned and actual house demolition in each province
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 2,138 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report gives two separate province figures for households affected by house demolition - 82 in Hunan, counted as 321 people, and 243 in Gansu, counted as 681 people - and prints no total of the two. Of the Gansu figure, 230 households and 613 people were at Hongwansi town of Zhangye, where the report records that resettlement and compensation were completed before the project began, so the demolition the project itself caused in Gansu is the remaining 13 households. Separately 471 households in Hunan and 640 in Gansu were affected by land acquisition without their houses being taken.
hunan-gansu-small-towns-demolition.outcome: The three loans closed on 31 December 2018, a year late, with US$148.43 million of US$150 million disbursed. The completion report of 24 September 2019 rates relevance high, efficacy modest and efficiency substantial. The Independent Evaluation Group's review rates the outcome Moderately Unsatisfactory, and rates the results framework weak on the ground that all the objective-level indicators were in substance intermediate outcome indicators.

wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.title: A Household Moved for a Hospital Resettled Into a Landslide Zone in Wushan County
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.place: Wushan Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital site and the Heiliangzi Residential Site, Wushan county, Chongqing municipality, China
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.point: Wushan county, Chongqing, the county holding both the hospital construction site and the Heiliangzi Residential Site (OpenStreetMap place point for 巫山县, Chongqing)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-81710 for the Chongqing Urban Rural Integration Project II-Health (P126210). US$100 million approved 14 June 2012, effective 5 October 2012; the commitment was revised to US$86,908,585 and that amount was disbursed. Original closing 31 August 2017, actual closing 31 January 2021. Total project cost fell from US$155,510,000 to US$140,798,585. Environmental category B; the policies triggered included Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01), Physical Cultural Resources (OP/BP 4.11) and Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12). The borrower was the People's Republic of China and the implementing agency the Chongqing project management office. The completion report rates the overall outcome Moderately Satisfactory, on Substantial relevance, Substantial efficacy and Modest efficiency, and records that the overall safeguards rating was Satisfactory in most implementation status reports but was downgraded to Moderately Satisfactory in the last two because of the pending safeguard issues from the landslide. The Independent Evaluation Group's review ICRR0022804 also rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and rates the quality of the completion report High (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00005207, 29 October 2021, data sheet and paragraphs 46, 73 to 75 and Box 2; IEG ICR Review ICRR0022804).

companies.name: Chongqing project management office
companies.role: The municipal government unit that ran the project, with a project implementation unit in Wushan county beneath it. The Wushan unit suspended the hospital civil works and evacuated the construction workers when the landslide happened, and the county government, headed by a deputy county mayor, took on the landslide treatment works, the monitoring and the emergency plan (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 29 October 2021, data sheet, Box 2 and footnote 10).

wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.community: The loan paid for hospital works in Chongqing, including civil works in four buildings of the Wushan Traditional Chinese Medicine Hospital. Land acquisition and resettlement were in the end needed only for that hospital, where they economically affected 52 households with 186 people and physically affected 31 households with 116 people. By the time the project closed the resettlement of 29 households had been completed. Two households remained to be followed up after closing. One had accepted a resettlement apartment at the Heiliangzi Residential Site, then changed its mind and chose to wait for a new apartment being built at the Longsheng Residential Site, and in the meantime was receiving rental and transitional payment support under the resettlement plan. The other was settled at the Heiliangzi Residential Site, which lies inside the landslide-affected area. In June 2018 a landslide, which the completion report attributes primarily to heavy rainfall, affected two of the hospital's buildings and two of the five residential buildings in that area, buildings the county government had put up to resettle people affected by various projects in the county. No people were living in the landslide area at the time. Three of the five residential buildings there passed an acceptance test in June 2019 and households moved into them afterwards; the household resettled by this project moved into its home in that area in July 2020 and was living there when the completion report was written. The report states that the ongoing monitoring and technical advice confirmed the building was well within safety limits in terms of movement, and that the household confirmed it had received all the compensation and allowance identified in the resettlement plan. The Independent Evaluation Group's review, written later, states instead that 'there are persisting risks related to uncertainties in landslide stabilization affecting one new hospital site in Wushan', that the local government has spent over US$10 million on stabilisation, and that 'the landslide has not been effectively stabilized and the risk of deterioration remains.' The first phase of treatment works was expected to be completed by June 2022 and the assessment of whether a second phase was needed was to follow after June 2023. The Bank stopped supervising the project from 1 October 2021.
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.displaced_label: 29 households whose resettlement was complete at project closing, of 31 households physically affected, from the Bank's completion report
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 744 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report counts 31 households with 116 people physically affected by land acquisition and resettlement at the Wushan hospital site, of which 29 had completed resettlement at closing and two had not.
wushan-hospital-landslide-resettlement.outcome: The loan closed on 31 January 2021, three years and five months late, with US$86.91 million of the US$100 million disbursed and the commitment cut to that amount. Construction of the Wushan hospital was suspended in 2018 after the landslide and had not resumed when the completion report was written. The completion report of 29 October 2021 and the Independent Evaluation Group's review both rate the overall outcome Moderately Satisfactory. The household this project resettled was living in a building inside the landslide-affected area, which the completion report says is within safety limits and which the review says sits in a landslide that has not been effectively stabilised.

lenders.role: Loan IBRD-82700 for the Anhui Xuancheng Infrastructure for Industry Relocation Project (P129431). companies.name: Xuancheng Economic and Technological Development Zone Management Committee
companies.role: The zone authority, a body of the Xuancheng municipal government, which the completion report names as taking the corrective measures after the fatal accident and as running the zone's resettlement office. The zone was set up in 1996 as a 6.24 square kilometre industrial park, expanded by a further 17 square kilometres by the local government, and the project financed its Phase 2 infrastructure (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 23 February 2021, paragraphs 4 and 93 to 94).

companies.name: Xuancheng project management office
companies.role: The municipal project office that managed implementation, prepared and disclosed the resettlement action plan, ran the grievance mechanism and hired the external environmental management and resettlement monitoring consultants. After the fatal accident it strengthened its safety processes and required special construction inspections and monthly personnel training (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 23 February 2021, data sheet, paragraph 93 and Annex 7).

xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.community: The loan paid for roads, a wastewater treatment plant and other infrastructure in the Xuancheng development zone, built so that factories moving inland from China's coast could relocate there. The resettlement action plan of 3 April 2013 had provided for the demolition of private houses of 161 households, 38,049.17 square metres in total, of which 9,719.61 square metres were brick-concrete and 23,631.98 square metres brick-wood. Because some subprojects were changed or cancelled, houses of 86 households were demolished, and a footnote to the completion report puts the area at 23,747 square metres: 'Of the planned 38,049 m2 of houses, only 23,747 m2 of houses were eventually demolished, belonging to 86 households, which received compensation as required.' The plan had provided for permanent land acquisition of 2,558.1 mu, of which 1,676.18 mu was cultivated land; at closing 1,984.15 mu had been acquired, excluding five roads cancelled late in the project. The completion report states that the compensation process was transparent and satisfactory, that the information disclosure policy was implemented well, that the affected people's living conditions were not affected by the project, and that in 2015 a large number of new apartments were distributed to people affected by the land expropriation, whose living conditions greatly improved. A grievance mechanism was run by the project office with information boards in the villages and complaint points at the land acquisition office, the subdistrict offices and the zone's resettlement office, with the mayor's hotline, letters and visits as further channels; the report says the complaints were few and that the main one concerned the technical design of the wastewater outfall, which was revised. A fatal accident occurred at a road construction site: a crane operator died when the crane fell over. A cause analysis found the accident occurred during the unloading of steel bars from a truck. The completion report adds that it 'was not considered noncompliance by the World Bank since adequate environmental safeguards had been established for the project.' The project office strengthened its safety processes afterwards and the report records that no more serious accidents occurred during implementation.
xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.displaced_label: 86 households whose houses were demolished, from the Bank's completion report and its footnote 38
xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 2,053 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report counts 86 households whose private houses were demolished, 23,747 square metres, against a resettlement plan that provided for 161 households and 38,049.17 square metres. No Bank document found gives a count of people as against households.
xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.killed_note: One death: a crane operator killed when the crane fell over at a project road construction site. The completion report's cause analysis places the accident during the unloading of steel bars from a truck, and the report adds that the Bank did not consider it non-compliance because adequate environmental safeguards had been established for the project. Neither the completion report nor the Evaluation Group's review attributes the death to a named failure of site safety management.
xuancheng-industry-zone-house-demolition.outcome: The loan closed on 31 August 2020, almost two years late, with US$87.28 million of the US$150 million disbursed and the commitment cut to that amount. Lower-than-planned land acquisition and resettlement costs, together with lower bids, produced US$4.6 million of savings in mid-2018 that were reallocated to other activities. The completion report of 23 February 2021 and the Independent Evaluation Group's review both rate the overall outcome Satisfactory on a split rating.

moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.title: Forest Land Flooded by the Moba Gorge Dam Paid for at a Fraction of the Agreed Rate
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.place: Moba Gorge dam and reservoir, Cheng county, Longnan municipality, Gansu province, China, with earthquake recovery works across 23 counties and districts of Gansu and Sichuan
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.point: Cheng county, Longnan municipality, Gansu, the county holding the Moba Gorge dam and reservoir and the water treatment plant it was built to supply (OpenStreetMap place point for 成县, Longnan)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan IBRD-76160 for the Wenchuan Earthquake Recovery Project (P114107). US$710 million approved 12 February 2009, effective 17 June 2009, of which US$695.80 million was disbursed. The lending instrument was an Emergency Recovery Loan prepared under OP/BP 8.00, Rapid Response to Crises and Emergencies. Original closing 30 June 2014, actual closing 31 May 2016, after restructurings on 19 November 2012, 16 June 2014 and 23 January 2015. Environmental category A; the policies the completion report names as triggered are Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01), Natural Habitats (OP/BP 4.04), Indigenous Peoples (OP/BP 4.10), Physical Cultural Resources, Involuntary Resettlement and Safety of Dams (OP/BP 4.37), with the review noting that the completion report cites the resettlement policy as OD 4.30 where the emergency project paper cites OP/BP 4.12. The borrower was the People's Republic of China; the implementing agencies were the Longnan Municipal Government and the Gansu Provincial Government, and the Sichuan Provincial Construction Commission and Sichuan Provincial Health Bureau. The French Development Agency was a co-financier. The completion report rates the outcome Satisfactory, Bank performance Satisfactory, borrower performance Satisfactory, implementing agency performance Moderately Satisfactory, risk to development outcome Substantial, and the involuntary resettlement safeguard satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group's review ICRR0020667 rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report ICR00003783, 27 February 2017, data sheet sections A, B and C and paragraphs 49 to 51 and Annex 6; IEG ICR Review ICRR0020667).

companies.name: Longnan Municipal Government
companies.role: One of the project's implementing agencies, the municipal government in Gansu whose project management office engaged the consultants that monitored and supervised the land acquisition and resettlement for the Moba Gorge dam and the other Longnan works. The completion report records that it was the Longnan municipal government that agreed at loan closure to acquire the forest land permanently in accordance with the approved resettlement plan (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 27 February 2017, data sheet and paragraphs 49 to 50 and Annex 6 paragraph 9).

moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.community: The loan paid for roads, bridges, embankments, water supply, wastewater treatment and health and education facilities in villages across 23 counties and districts, 16 in Sichuan and 7 in Gansu, after the 2008 earthquake. The completion report's table of actual completed land acquisition and impacts records 213,373.62 square metres of housing demolished, affecting 1,081 households and 3,435 people: 111,473.4 square metres, 539 households and 1,454 people in Sichuan across three batches, and 101,900.22 square metres, 542 households and 1,981 people in Gansu. The largest single demolition was 107,014.6 square metres in Sichuan's second batch, affecting 515 households and 1,347 people, and 101,203.63 square metres in Longnan, affecting 539 households and 1,965 people. At the Moba Gorge dam itself 696.59 square metres of housing was demolished, affecting three households and 16 people, and 1,018 mu of land was acquired, affecting 66 households and 313 people. Across the project 4,266.47 mu, or 284 hectares, of land was permanently acquired, affecting 3,142 households and 12,228 people, with a further 132.1 hectares taken temporarily during construction; land acquisition and compensation cost about US$84.82 million, 557.29 million yuan. The resettlement objective set in the approved plans was to achieve equal or better income and living standards, the compensation rate for houses was to include the value of the house, moving costs and compensation for permanent attachments, and where residential housing was demolished the households were to be paid replacement cost without depreciation, with a choice of cash, property exchange or self-reconstruction in the resettlement area. For the Moba Gorge reservoir, however, compensation was paid below the rate the Bank-approved plan required. That plan required the permanent acquisition of 635.49 mu of forest land to be flooded by the reservoir, at between 3,160 yuan per mu for the 188.9 mu designated as forested and 1,744 yuan per mu for the 554.55 mu designated as unused waste land. The completion report records that 'the actual compensation paid was much less and based on the lease value of the land (RMB 10 per mu per annum for 65 years i.e. RMB650/mu)', and that the compensation 'was below agreed rates'. The issue was not resolved before the loan closed. At closure the Bank insisted and the Longnan municipal government agreed to acquire the land permanently in accordance with the approved plan, and the Bank said it would keep monitoring. The Evaluation Group's review records that the issue remained pending as of January 2017 and was expected to be resolved only by the end of 2017. Resettlement difficulties in Gansu also forced roads to be realigned or replaced and delayed the Moba Gorge dam, whose works and associated water treatment plant were delayed 23 months; the completion report attributes part of this to slow government decision-making and funding for resettlement and to poor communication with stakeholders. The completion report states that for the rest of the project the external monitoring showed all affected people were fully compensated in accordance with the plans, that all permanent and temporary compensation was paid on time, that compensation for temporary land use equalled or exceeded the plans, and that living standards of the affected people improved. It also records separately, as a social benefit, that where it was unsafe to rebuild existing communities in place, about 5,000 households from the worst affected communities were resettled as communities in new housing, and that surveys found a high level of satisfaction with those arrangements.
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.displaced_label: 1,081 affected households, 3,435 people, whose housing was demolished, from the Bank's completion report table of actual completed land acquisition and impacts
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 705 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report's table of actual completed impacts counts 213,373.62 square metres of housing demolished affecting 1,081 households and 3,435 people, and separately 4,266.47 mu of land permanently acquired affecting 3,142 households and 12,228 people, for a total of 3,711 affected households and 14,218 people. The report also records that about 5,000 households from the worst affected communities were resettled in new housing because it was unsafe to rebuild in place after the earthquake; that is a hazard relocation the report presents as a benefit of the project and it is not included in the figure above.
moba-gorge-forest-land-compensation.outcome: The loan closed on 31 May 2016, almost two years late, with US$695.80 million of the US$710 million disbursed. The completion report of 27 February 2017 rates the outcome Satisfactory and the involuntary resettlement safeguard satisfactory; the Independent Evaluation Group's review rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory. The forest land for the Moba Gorge reservoir had not been permanently acquired at loan closing and the compensation paid was 650 yuan per mu against the 1,744 to 3,160 yuan per mu the approved plan set. The review records that the matter remained pending as of January 2017 and was expected to be settled only by the end of 2017. The Moba Gorge dam was substantially completed as of December 2016 and the Bank accepted the government's assurance of continued supervision and a final independent dam safety review after completion.

zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.title: Families at the Zhamushui Dam Left Waiting Years for Resettlement in Jianshi County
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.place: Zhamushui and Hongwawu hydropower stations on the Guangrun river, Jianshi county, Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Hubei province, China
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.point: Jianshi county seat, Enshi prefecture, the county holding both dams; the completion report notes the Zhamushui dam is close to the county town (OpenStreetMap place point for 建始县, Enshi Tujia and Miao Autonomous Prefecture)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: The works were a fifth component of the Hubei Hydropower Development in Poor Areas Project (P068049, Loan 4666-CHA), approved by the Board in June 2002, paid for out of about US$16 million of loan savings on the four original components. The Loan Agreement was amended in July 2006 to add the Guangrun component and a Project Agreement for it was prepared in January 2007; the amendment's listed activities include 'Compensation, resettlement, and rehabilitation of project-affected persons (PAPs).' The change was approved by the Regional Vice President. The carbon finance operation's own data sheet records the Bank lending or grant figure for the component as US$15.97 million. The loan closing date was extended in June 2010 to accommodate the component's delay, and the Loan Agreement was amended again in March 2011 after a change of ownership; the second closing extension of 18 months ran to 31 December 2011. The component's total installed capacity is 28.4 MW and the estimated investment 276 million yuan, about US$33 million; it suffered a cost overrun of US$32.86 million, exceeding its 2006 appraisal estimate by 90 per cent, which the completion report attributes in part to the 'increased cost of resettlement, which was mostly incurred after the World Bank loan closed in 2011.' Environmental category A; the policies triggered were Environmental Assessment (OP/BP 4.01), Natural Habitats (OP/BP 4.04), Involuntary Resettlement (OP/BP 4.12) and Safety of Dams (OP/BP 4.37). The carbon finance completion report rates outcomes Unsatisfactory, Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory and project entity performance Moderately Unsatisfactory, and rates efficacy for the loan project Modest and efficiency Negligible (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report No. 153668 on a Purchase of Emission Reductions from the Community Development Carbon Fund, 14 October 2020, data sheet and paragraphs 2, 5 to 8, 16, 32 to 35 and 79 to 88).

lenders.name: Community Development Carbon Fund, World Bank
lenders.role: The carbon fund that signed an Emission Reductions Purchase Agreement with the Guangrun company (P094795) on 27 October 2006, effective the same day, amended on 3 October 2012 and 18 May 2015 and terminated on 30 June 2018. The contracted volume was 157,745 certified emission reductions, of which 145,699 were actually delivered; the third monitoring period delivered 94,924 against 104,970 contracted. The agreement included an advance payment of US$388,000, 2.44 million yuan in 2006, on the carbon credits, to fund part of a community benefit plan addressing poverty alleviation in nine villages affected by the component. This was a purchase of emission reductions, not a loan for the works (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 14 October 2020, data sheet sections A, B and F and paragraphs 27 to 28).

companies.name: Guodian Guangrun Hydropower Development Company Ltd.
companies.role: The project entity that built and owns the two dams and three power stations. Its main sponsor until May 2010 was Guoxin Company, holding 55 per cent of the shares, which then sold them to Guodian Company, one of China's five large state-owned power generation companies. The completion report records that the entity stopped paying the World Bank loan and its interest from 2013, about 8 million yuan a year, after which the Jianshi county government paid it, amounting to more than 30 million yuan as of early 2019; that Guodian has classified the project as negative assets; and that Guodian was in negotiation to sell it back to Jianshi county (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 14 October 2020, data sheet, paragraph 15, footnote 6 and paragraphs 34 and 89).

companies.name: Jianshi County Government
companies.role: The county government in Enshi prefecture, Hubei, which submitted the 2011 report asking for the resettlement compensation rates to be adjusted and whose approval in October 2011 preceded the first relocations. It failed to provide the financial support agreed at appraisal of the component, never paid for the water supply service, and from 2013 took over paying the Bank loan and interest. The county's resettlement bureau was the local body handling resettlement (World Bank Implementation Completion and Results Report, 14 October 2020, paragraphs 86 and 89 and footnote 6; World Bank Independent Evaluation Group Project Performance Assessment Report, 18 June 2018, Annex listing persons met).

zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.community: The component built a 41.5 metre concrete slab rock-fill dam and two powerhouses at Hongwawu and a 77.5 metre concrete double-curvature arch dam and powerhouse at Zhamushui on the Guangrun river in Jianshi county, plus transmission lines and, later, a small station at Kongzishan. Resettlement took 164.5 hectares of land, of which 2.5 hectares was taken temporarily for construction, and 2,185 square metres of housing was demolished. Resettlement at Hongwawu was completed by 31 July 2010. At Zhamushui it was 'continuously postponed as price levels and other relative conditions changed'. In 2011 the Jianshi county government asked for the resettlement compensation rates for the acquired land to be adjusted, which was approved in October 2011. By November 2011 seven families at the dam area and six families in the reservoir area had been relocated. Fifteen families in the reservoir area had finished consultations but had not been relocated; their relocation took place in mid-June 2012. Compensation for land acquisition was completed in 2012, when resettlement documents and payment proofs were delivered to the Bank. The completion report attributes the early delays to 'contingency land occupation during project construction' and says 'it was hard to organize payments'. An information booklet to inform affected people of the resettlement policies and compensation rates was delayed and was only fully distributed by 2011. The completion report states that a Resettlement Independent Monitoring Group was hired to help and speed up the resettlement, that despite the delays resettlement was completed successfully according to that group, that the affected people were largely satisfied with the resettlement and compensation, and that their income level and quality of life were substantially improved. It records that the new housing was concrete and brick rather than brick, stone and wood, had water supply and electricity, and was closer to transport, schools, hospitals and shops, that all the relocated families received land and mountain forest with more favourable conditions for agriculture than before, and that the income of the directly affected people rose about 18.37 per cent against 2007. The nine affected villages also received a community benefit plan funded in part by the carbon advance payment, including village drinking water projects, and 20 per cent of the component's value added tax went to the Jianshi county poverty alleviation fund for six years from 2012 to 2017. Against that, the dams themselves have been troubled throughout. Significant leakage was found in the right bank of the Hongwawu dam; the first stage of treatment was completed on 31 August 2013 and the second stage had not begun when the completion report was written, with the entity intending to start only if a water dispute is resolved in its favour, while the Bank noted that in the monsoon season water can rise about 4 metres above the current treatment. Tailings from small coal mines upstream washed into the Hongwawu reservoir and silted it; the Guangrun river is the water source for the Jianshi county seat. At Zhamushui the left abutment was treated but no decision had been taken on the right abutment, which the Bank called a significant concern because the dam is so close to the county town, and the dam movement monitoring system at Hongwawu was not implemented, which the report says jeopardises dam safety. The dam safety panel appointed in May 2012 was not closely involved in the technical work and its report, due by May 2016, was produced only in May 2019 after numerous reminders. The county government never paid for the water supply service.
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.displaced_label: 28 families relocated at Zhamushui: seven at the dam area and six in the reservoir area by November 2011, and the 15 remaining reservoir-area families in mid-June 2012, from the Bank's completion report
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 848 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Bank's completion report counts the relocations at Zhamushui in three parts - seven families at the dam area, six families in the reservoir area, and 15 further reservoir-area families relocated in mid-June 2012 - and gives no total. It gives no count at all for the Hongwawu resettlement, which it says was completed by 31 July 2010, and it puts the housing demolished across the component at 2,185 square metres.
zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.outcome: Construction was still incomplete as of December 2019, with two water diversion tunnels and second-stage treatment of the Hongwawu reservoir's right bank outstanding and no decision taken on the Zhamushui right bank slope and crest spillway gates. The carbon purchase agreement terminated on 30 June 2018 having delivered 145,699 of 157,745 contracted certified emission reductions. The completion report of 14 October 2020 rates outcomes Unsatisfactory and efficiency for the loan project Negligible, finds the financial internal rate of return now below zero against 5.44 per cent at appraisal, and records that Guodian has classified the project as negative assets and was negotiating to sell it back to Jianshi county. The Bank reports all resettlement finalised and all affected people compensated.

zhamushui-guangrun-resettlement-postpone.confidence_note: The whole account rests on World Bank documents about the Bank's own operation: the 2020 completion report on the carbon purchase, which is also the only document found that reports the Guangrun resettlement outcome, together with the parent loan's 2012 completion report and the Independent Evaluation Group's 2018 Project Performance Assessment Report, neither of which gives the Guangrun resettlement counts. No independent press report, court record, audit or field study was found. The figure of 28 families is the sum of the three groups the completion report names separately at Zhamushui; the report prints no total and gives no count for Hongwawu, so the total number of families relocated across the component is not known. The money that carries the project's name, the Community Development Carbon Fund purchase agreement, bought emission reductions and did not pay for the works; the works were paid for out of savings on the parent IBRD loan, whose agreement was amended in July 2006 to add them and to include compensation, resettlement and rehabilitation of affected people among the activities financed. The documents report the affected people as satisfied and better off; what they record as going wrong is the repeated postponement of the Zhamushui resettlement, the delayed compensation and information booklet, and the dam safety and leakage problems that remain. The completion report's data sheet gives its ICR date as 30 September 2020 while the cover page is dated 14 October 2020.

wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.title: 7,312 Households Moved for Wuhan's Roads, Three Times the Number Planned
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.place: Wuhan, Hubei province, China, including the Sanjintan to Ping'anpu section of the Middle Ring road
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.point: Sanjintan, Houhu subdistrict, Jiang'an district, Wuhan, the northern end of the Middle Ring section whose resettlement plan of July 2007 covered 294 households (OpenStreetMap point for 三金潭, Houhu subdistrict, Jiang'an district, Wuhan)

lenders.name: World Bank (IBRD)
lenders.role: Loan L4727 for the Wuhan Urban Transport Project (P069852). US$200 million approved 9 March 2004, signed and conformed 12 May 2004, of which US$199 million was disbursed, with a US$1 million front-end fee. Original closing 30 June 2009, extended by one year to 30 June 2010 to complete unfinished activities and because of delays in the resettlement process. A Japanese grant, TF026239, had funded preparation from September 2001. The project was category A because of substantial new construction and considerable involuntary resettlement. Total project cost net of the front-end fee rose by US$713 million, of which a US$321 million increase in the cost of resettlement was the largest single factor; the borrower contribution rose 279 per cent from US$398.20 million to US$1,110.66 million. The executing agency was the Wuhan Municipal Government, with the Wuhan Urban Transport Project Office under the Wuhan Municipal Capital Investment Management Office managing implementation. The Independent Evaluation Group's review reports that the completion report rated the outcome Satisfactory and rates it Moderately Satisfactory itself, rates Bank performance Moderately Satisfactory against the report's Satisfactory, and rates government, implementing agency and overall borrower performance Moderately Satisfactory; it records that the Bank's Quality Assurance Group rated quality at entry satisfactory in seven of nine areas assessed and moderately satisfactory in two, one of them the resettlement process (Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR13574, posted 27 June 2011; World Bank Project Appraisal Document Report No. 25590, 12 February 2004).

companies.name: Wuhan Municipal Capital Investment Management Office
companies.role: The municipal body with overall responsibility for preparing and implementing the project, under the Wuhan Municipal Government. The Wuhan Urban Transport Project Office sat under it and managed and coordinated implementation; the Wuhan Bridge Construction Company, a unit of the same office, was responsible for the road infrastructure component, and a separate Resettlement Office for the project prepared the resettlement action plans (World Bank Project Appraisal Document, 12 February 2004, paragraphs 4.1 and 4.3; Wuhan Urban Transport Project, Resettlement Action Plan RP603, July 2007).

companies.name: Wuhan Public Transport Group Company
companies.role: The municipal bus operator, which the Evaluation Group's review records failed to implement 13 of 37 public transport infrastructure subprojects, attributing that to land acquisition and timing issues and to the company's resistance to further reform of public transport bus franchising (Independent Evaluation Group ICR Review ICRR13574, 27 June 2011).

wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.community: The loan paid for new and widened roads, interchanges, pedestrian facilities, traffic management, bus facilities and road maintenance across Wuhan. The appraisal document of February 2004 stated that 'Housing demolition will require relocation of 1,164 urban households and 1,064 suburban households', and its annex put the total number of people required to relocate their residence at 9,072, in 2,478 households. The Evaluation Group's review of the completion report records the outcome: 'Resettlement was a highly complex and sensitive task necessitating the acquisition of 375 hectares of land, 1.45 million square m. of various structures, and the relocation of 7,312 households.' That is close to three times the number of households the appraisal planned for. The total cost of implementing the resettlement plan reached US$514 million, which the review says was nearly twice the amount estimated at appraisal, and was funded entirely by the borrower; the reasons the review gives are changes in the project's scope, rising land costs and the appreciation of the Chinese renminbi. The review records that the loan closing was extended by a year in part because of delays in the resettlement process, that land acquisition problems and timing were among the reasons eight of eleven passenger interchanges and five of twelve terminals were dropped from the public transport component, and that four roads and two interchanges were dropped because traffic volumes were low. One subproject plan, for the Sanjintan to Ping'anpu section of the Middle Ring road, was prepared in July 2007 and covered 294 households with 1,268 members, 70,612.43 square metres of private housing, and five enterprises and institutions with 3,817.62 square metres, after a design change had already cut the households to be moved by 106 and the housing area by 4,566 square metres. The review also records the favourable side of the completion report's account: that according to the report Wuhan University regards the process as a model of good practice for other cities in China; that the report says the project complied with the Bank's environmental and social safeguard policies, 'while the evidence indicates that many people are actually better off after the resettlement'; and that of about 1,000 residents interviewed on environmental impacts, some 95 per cent expressed satisfaction with the mitigation measures. It notes that the steps taken are discussed in Annex 4 of the completion report. One procurement case, concerning the Changqing interchange, was referred to the Bank's Institutional Integrity unit; the review says the completion report gives no details of the allegations and that the investigation did not reveal improper practice.
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.displaced_label: 7,312 households relocated, as the Independent Evaluation Group's review reports the Bank's completion report
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.displaced_note: ICIJ gives 1,297 for this project, which is its count of project-affected people and not a count of people moved. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of the completion report gives 7,312 households relocated, against the appraisal document's plan of 1,164 urban and 1,064 suburban households, or 2,478 households and 9,072 people in total. No Bank document found gives a count of people relocated as against households, and the 1.45 million square metres of structures acquired is a structure figure, not a count of people.
wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.outcome: The loan closed on 30 June 2010, a year late, with US$199 million of US$200 million disbursed. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 27 June 2011 rates the outcome Moderately Satisfactory and reports that the completion report rated it Satisfactory. The resettlement, three times the size planned, was paid for entirely by Wuhan at US$514 million, nearly twice the appraisal estimate, and was the largest single reason the project's cost rose by US$713 million. A second project, the China Wuhan Second Urban Transport Project (P112838), followed in 2010.

wuhan-middle-ring-resettlement-overrun.confidence_note: The outcome figures here rest on a single document, and on a document that is itself a summary of one that cannot be read. The Bank's own Implementation Completion and Results Report for this project is not disclosed: it is absent from the Bank's document search under its own project number and under a title search, and the only route to its content is the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 27 June 2011, which cites it by page. Every outcome figure above - 7,312 households relocated, 375 hectares, 1.45 million square metres of structures, the US$514 million resettlement cost and the US$321 million increase - comes from that review and not from a document that can be read directly. The appraisal plan figures, by contrast, were read in the appraisal document itself, so the gap between plan and outcome is documented at one end only. No independent press report, court record, audit or field study of the Wuhan resettlement was found. The review also reports that the completion report found compliance with the Bank's safeguard policies, that many people were better off after the resettlement, and that Wuhan University called the process a model of good practice; those claims cannot be checked either. Because the review prints a column for the completion report's own ratings and that column has been wrong on other projects, the Satisfactory outcome rating above is given as what the review reports the completion report to have said.

drop-p087291-jincheng-cbm.title: CN-PCF Jincheng Coal Bed Methane Project

drop-p100968-shanxi-cbm.title: Shanxi Coal Bed Methane Development and Utilization
drop-p100968-shanxi-cbm.drop_reason: Screened out on the project's own resettlement action plan of 27 March 2008, which says at paragraph 1 'No house demolition and relocation would be required' and at section 3.3 'No demolition and relocation will be involved.' drop-p121263-gef-eco-transport.title: China GEF City Cluster Eco-Transport Project
drop-p121263-gef-eco-transport.drop_reason: Dropped on what the money financed. The completion report of 26 December 2016 states at paragraph 16 'The Grant financed technical assistance, advisory and capacity building services' and at paragraph 37 'The GEF grant of US$4.8 million (US$4.53 disbursed) paid for consultant services and IT goods.' On the outcome the report states that post-project interviews confirmed compensation rates, procedures and consultation were as promised in the plan, that no complaints were received, and that external monitoring showed incomes rose after land acquisition and resettlement. drop-p129563-anhui-yellow-mountain.title: Anhui Yellow Mountain New Countryside Demonstration Project
drop-p129563-anhui-yellow-mountain.drop_reason: Screened out on the completion report's own outcome statement. drop-p099224-liaoning-third-medium-citie.title: Liaoning Third Medium Cities Infrastructure
drop-p099224-liaoning-third-medium-citie.drop_reason: Dropped because no document counts anyone actually relocated. The appraisal document expected the project to affect 956 persons from 308 households through permanent land acquisition, temporary land use and demolition of housing, as the Independent Evaluation Group's review of 18 October 2017 records at page 17 of the appraisal document, and the resettlement plan of December 2007 plans for 562 persons in 179 households affected by urban residential house demolition in the Benxi and Yangjiazhangzi subprojects, 6,979.55 square metres. Those are plan figures. The completion report of 20 December 2016 gives no demolition or relocation outcome at all: paragraphs 61 and 62 record that resettlement plans were prepared and approved for the Yingkou Dashiqiao, Benxi Nanfen and Huludao subprojects, that none of the four subprojects added at restructuring involved land acquisition, that for the Chaoyang subproject a due diligence review confirmed the associated combined heat and power site had completed its land acquisition and resettlement before joining the project, and that according to the project office's monitoring reports 'all affected people were compensated for land acquisition and rehabilitation measures in accordance with the RAPs'. The later resettlement documents of 2010, 2012, 2013 and the revised policy framework of June 2014 carry no outcome figures either. The project also closed small coal boilers; the report records efforts to redeploy the affected boiler workers into heat supply companies with skill training, with no count of job losses. Loan of US$191 million approved 27 May 2008.

drop-p111325-dashiqiao-heating.title: Dashiqiao Central Heating Supply Project
drop-p111325-dashiqiao-heating.drop_reason: Dropped on what the money financed and on the absence of any outcome document. The implementation status report of 19 December 2014 states 'This is a subproject under Liaoning Third Medium Cities Infrastructure Project (P099224)', and the project information document of 9 December 2009 describes a carbon offset operation whose board approval date is given as the emission reductions purchase agreement of 31 December 2009, with the development objectives being to improve the energy efficiency and environmental performance of heating in Dashiqiao and to reduce carbon dioxide emissions. The two documents filed as the project's resettlement plans are both volumes of RP590, the Liaoning Medium Cities Infrastructure Project resettlement policy framework, which is the parent project's instrument. No completion report exists for P111325; the Bank's document list holds 15 items, the latest the 2014 status report. A purchase of emission reductions is not a loan for the works, and the works' own project, P099224, is itself dropped above for want of any count of people relocated.

drop-p093882-shandong-fgd.title: Shandong Flue Gas Desulfurization
drop-p093882-shandong-fgd.drop_reason: Screened out because the two subprojects that needed land were never built and the one that was built needed none. The Independent Evaluation Group's review of 9 June 2015 states that resettlement action plans were developed and disclosed for the two newly constructed power plants, Yantai Bajiao and Laiwu, and that 'The other two construction of FGD facilities were proposed to be located within existing power plants (Huangtai and Lubei) with no new land acquisition and resettlement.' It then states 'Of the four selected power plants, only the Lubei plant was partially implemented' and that the Lubei subproject 'was subsequently cancelled due to the discovery of fraudulent practices', which the completion report of 21 December 2012 confirms at paragraph 34. So the only works that went ahead sat inside an existing power plant. The review notes that there is no social safeguards section in the completion report to reference Lubei's position. The documents' recorded irregularity is the fraud that killed the subproject and an environmental management plan updated late after a change from a calcium-based to a magnesium-based desulfurisation technology, with no evidence of disclosure of the update; neither is harm to identifiable people. Loan of US$50 million approved 27 May 2008.

drop-p112626-liuzhou-environment-ii.title: Liuzhou Environment Management Project Phase II
drop-p112626-liuzhou-environment-ii.drop_reason: Dropped because no dwelling was taken and no one is counted as relocated. The project's social assessment of 25 May 2010 states that the Shatang, Guantang and Sanjiang sewage treatment plants involve land acquisition 'but no house demolition is involved'. The updated resettlement plan of October 2015, which does carry outcome figures, records that 117.24 mu of rural collective land was permanently acquired, affecting 57 households with 255 persons in Jila village, Yangjiaoshan town, Yufeng district and Baisha village, Jingxiu subdistrict, Liubei district, against 107.9 mu planned; and that 8,134.9 square metres of structures were demolished affecting 23 households with 118 persons, against 2,503.9 square metres planned. What was demolished, however, was not housing: at Longquanshan the plan calls the structures 'rural field attendance houses (non-residential)', 18 households and 87 persons, and at Baisha the 5,631.01 square metres affecting 5 households and 31 persons were the premises of five entities - Liuzhou Jinhui Material Recycling Co., Ltd., Huangsheng Pig-raising Equipment Co., Ltd., an equipment lease warehouse, the Longyue Baisha car park, and prefabricated buildings housing a construction team - in an additional 19.13 mu acquired for urban landscaping and road construction. The plan records that the affected households were compensated for. The completion report of 21 February 2019 reports no relocation and states at paragraph 79 that 'Independent reviews showed that livelihoods of affected persons have fully recovered or became better off after the completion of land acquisition and resettlement', with challenges and delays in land acquisition arising from legacy issues and the city's urbanisation master plans. Round 20's rule applies: an outcome of land area plus a count of affected people, with no dwelling lost, is not a specific harm to identifiable people. The figures are recorded here so that the lead can reverse this if the five demolished business premises are judged to be trading places taken. Phase I of this project, P081346, is already on the map as liuzhou-environment-management-resettlement; this is a separate loan of US$150 million approved 10 March 2011.
